A lot of management just comes down to:

Tell them what you want
Show them how to do it
Check in to make sure they did
Give feedback on the outcome

And just doing that until you die.
items.transcript: There's three things that have to happen in order for you to be obligated to enforce a standard, which is that number one, someone has to know the standard you have. Number two is that they have to have the ability to adhere to that standard. And then three, choose not to. The consequence for crossing you needs to be consistent, which means that every time someone crosses you, there needs to be a consequence. If there isn't, then you teach people to gamble with you because it's a variable reinforcer. And so it has to be consistent. It has to be immediate. It has to be escalating, which means if the first time I tell you, I say, don't worry, you're with us. Be here tomorrow. Do better. Fine. If you do it again, then it's like you're off for the night. Because what happens is at some moment, it stops being about punishing the behavior and it should be about punishing the pattern of behavior. And so at that point, you have to respect the standard for everyone. And out of owing it to everyone, we have to let this person go, even if they're a perceived high performer.
